findings.reason: a node implementing this literally writes a status no reader consults, and the missed-rubric-item defect §40 exists to close survives the repair; the section must either name the predicate change that makes `absent_items` (or a chosen status) refuse coverage, or drop the readiness half as an inert field write.
findings.text: §40's deliverable says a delivered review whose `absent_items` is not empty "takes a status the coverage predicate does not count", but no plan-review reader keys on the stored `status`: `review_coverage` (`reckon/crew/plan_review.py:797`) matches stored reviews to plan content by `plan_fingerprint` and section digests alone, and the dispatch gate `require_plan_reviewed` (`reckon/crew/routing.py:2489`) judges a review only through `review_coverage` plus `unanswered_findings` and `review_lifecycle.is_hot` (`reckon/crew/review_lifecycle.py:265`), none of which read `status`. `PLAN_REVIEW_STATUSES` (`reckon/crew/plan_review.py:210`) is referenced nowhere else in the tree. A review with `absent_items: ['anchors_resolve']` and zero findings therefore still satisfies the gate — `unanswered_findings` returns empty and its fingerprint matches — whatever status it is stored under, so choosing a status other than `ready` changes nothing the coordinator or the gate reads. The section's stated purpose, "so the coordinator recomposes the review rather than building on it", is not reached by the change it prescribes.

findings.reason: a control that cannot fire leaves the node's gate measuring nothing, so the second half of §40 can be reported green without the behaviour it claims to guard.
findings.text: the readiness bullet "a report missing one rubric item stores with a status the coverage predicate does not count" cannot fail as written: because the coverage predicate counts no status, every status the node could write satisfies the missing-item case, and the case would pass on the unfixed code just as on the fixed code. The declared negative control for this half — "store every delivered review as `ready` again, and the absent-item case reads as coverage" — cannot redden for the same reason: `ready` is not what makes the review cover the plan (its fingerprint match is), so restoring it leaves the coverage verdict unchanged and the control passes on the mutation.

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: pass — `reckon/crew/review.py:1249` names `_PLAN_RUBRIC_LINE_RE`/`_PLAN_FINDING_LINE_RE`, `reckon/crew/plan_review.py:211` names `DEFAULT_STATUS = "ready"`, and the record builder sits at `plan_review.py:2099-2114`; no anchor names a deleted target.
rubric_items.done_when: a finding — the readiness case's declared negative control cannot fire, so the second half of §40's measure cannot fail as written.
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — the gate logs live under the run directory and the fragment under `docs/evidence/fragments/`, both durable paths, no scratchpad.
rubric_items.naming: pass — no plan label, stage name or ticket number reaches a symbol, filename or comment in §40's stated write paths.
rubric_items.reasoning: a finding — §40's readiness mechanism rests on the coverage predicate counting a stored status, and it counts none, so the mechanism does not produce the section's own goal.
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — §40 carries the same two halves an earlier review on this plan ruled one verdict on, and this round's edits (dropping the receipt clause, changing the readiness bullet) do not change that ruling.
rubric_items.wiring: pass — §40 declares no `depends-on`, `informs` or `gates` edge and needs none: it amends behaviour of already-`done` §§36–37, and its two cross-references (the §37 receipt field, the §34 node id) are explicitly placed outside this section.
